name: Beckey-Davis

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Alternate access only, used when the standard Stuart Lake Trailhead / Aasgard Pass approach is closed (e.g. wildfire closures) -- longer route via Snow Lakes/Lake Viviane (~10 mi one-way). Stuart Lake Trailhead is the standard/preferred access.
waypoints.directions: From US-2 at the western edge of Leavenworth, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FS Road 7601) and follow the rough dirt road 3.7 miles to the Stuart Lake Trailhead at about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park and overnight trips May 15 to Oct 31 need an Enchantment permit; the road is usually gated November into May.

waypoints.name: Gnome Tarn
waypoints.note: Landmark tarn on the boot path leading to the base of Prusik Peak's south face routes.
waypoints.directions: Take the Stuart Lake Trail about 2.5 miles to the Colchuck Lake Trail, cross Mountaineer Creek and climb to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft. From the boulder field at the lake's south end, climb Aasgard Pass, about 2,000 ft of loose scree in 1.25 miles, then cross the Core past Tranquil and Isolation lakes and go cross-country north over slabs and talus to Gnome Tarn below Prusik's south face.

waypoints.name: Prusik Peak south face base
waypoints.directions: Walk up from the tarn to the foot of the south face and find two large V-shaped features; the route starts in the chimney immediately left of them, to the right of the classic line in the middle of the face.

waypoints.name: Prusik Peak
waypoints.note: South Face route, 6-7 pitches, FA Beckey-Davis 1962.
waypoints.directions: Climb seven pitches, about 650 ft: left out of the chimney onto knobs, up face and cracks to Snafflehound Ledge, traverse right, take the 5.9 dihedral crux, then the crack and gully past a chockstone to the notch east of the summit horn, finishing with a friction traverse and jam crack to the summit.

approach: Standard access is via Aasgard Pass into the Core Enchantments: Stuart Lake Trailhead → Stuart Lake Trail (2.5 mi) → Colchuck Lake Trail #1599A, crossing Mountaineer Creek and switchbacking up to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft, ~4.1 mi/2,000 ft). From the south-end boulder field, climb Aasgard Pass (1.25 mi, ~2,000 ft of steep, loose scree/dirt — the crux of the approach, hazardous under lingering snow into early July with a hidden creek/moat beneath the talus, and avalanche-prone in shoulder season). From the 7,841-ft pass, travel cross-country through the Core past Isolation/Tranquil Lake toward Gnome Tarn and the base of Prusik's south face, roughly 7.5–8 miles and 4,600+ ft one-way. Note that this trailhead/pass can close seasonally (e.g., wildfire closures have forced parties onto the Snow Lakes Trail instead, which one trip report clocked at about 10 miles and 6,000+ ft, roughly 5 hours 44 minutes car-to-base — notably longer and with a different, less direct final approach past Lake Viviane to a climbers' trail on Prusik's south ridge).

approach_variants.name: Aasgard Pass and the Core to the chimney left of the two Vs
approach_variants.notes:
The Core Enchantments approach, shared with every other line on this face: Stuart Lake trailhead, Stuart Lake Trail to the Colchuck Lake Trail junction, across Mountaineer Creek and up to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft, then the boulder field at the south end and Aasgard Pass — 2,000 ft in 1.25 miles of loose scree, hazardous under lingering snow into early July because of a creek and moat hidden beneath it.

From the pass, cross-country north past Isolation and Tranquil Lake toward Gnome Tarn and the base of the south face, roughly 7.5 to 8 miles and 4,600 ft one way.

If the standard trailhead or the pass is shut — wildfire closures have done this — the Snow Lakes trail reaches the same face by a longer and less direct line past Lake Viviane and a climbers' path onto the south side of the peak. One party clocked that version at about ten miles and 6,000 ft.
hazards: Aasgard Pass: loose scree, and a hidden creek and moat under snow into early July
Avalanche on the pass in shoulder season
Unmarked cross-country travel for the final approach
Six rappels down the north face on ageing natural anchors — carry extra tat
A possible extra rappel from the West Ridge notch to regain the south-face base
Snafflehounds at the base will eat gear left unattended
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Look for two large Vs and start in the chimney to their left. That is the whole identification, it is published in exactly those terms, and the accompanying note is that you cannot miss it. Two prominent V-shaped features on the south face; the route's first pitch takes the chimney immediately left of them.

Confirm with the first pitch itself: from the chimney you move left and climb up on knobs to a belay, at about 5.7. Knobs after a leftward move out of a chimney is the signature. If you are pulling straight up out of the chimney with no traverse, look again.

Position relative to its neighbour, which is the check that catches the common error: this route is to the climber's right of the classic south-face line. So if you are at the middle of the base of the face, you are one route too far left. Walk right until the two Vs are on your right-hand side and you are at a chimney.

And a distance check on the route as a whole: seven pitches, about 650 ft, running 5.5 to 5.9, with a long chimney-gully crossing to a big ledge partway up and a forced rightward dihedral as the crux. A four- or five-pitch route ending on the West Ridge is one of the shorter lines on the left flank, not this.

In cloud, when you cannot see the Vs from a distance, walk the foot of the face and count chimneys rather than guessing: the Vs are large features and they are visible from close under them even when the summit is not.
